prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 公式文本 · 物理量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "物理量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 2: header "符号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "公式" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 91px
  col 4: header "单位" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 274px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact physics formula reference: for each quantity it gives the symbol, defining formula, unit and a short explanatory note, for lookup and quick comparison rather than continuous reading.","reading":"Readers scan row by row: quantity name → symbol → formula → unit, then drop into the note. Columns 2–4 form a compact technical core, while 说明 is secondary but contains constants and caveats that must remain legible.","groups":["Columns 2 符号, 3 公式 and 4 单位 belong together: they are the technical identity of each quantity and should stay adjacent and compact.","Column 1 物理量 is the row entry point and label.","Column 5 说明 is explanatory annotation and can absorb wrapping."],"keep_intact":["symbols such as E_k, F, E","formula tokens and operators; ideally whole formulas, at minimum unbreakable terms such as ½mv² and G·m₁m₂/r²","units J and N","scientific notation such as 6.674×10⁻¹¹","short headers 符号, 公式, 单位"],"may_wrap":["物理量 names such as 理想气体状态方程","说明 prose and notes","formulas at = or spaces if necessary, but not inside tokens"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [66, 52, 86, 52, 103] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [66, 52, 90, 52, 99] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [66, 54, 86, 54, 99] · table 360×392px · row heights [60, 83, 83, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
